podcast.title: More Into Rock
podcast.body: Craig Fuller eventually rejoined Pure Prairie League after his legal issues but did not remain with the band for long because he was "more into rock" than the collective direction the band wanted to pursue. This musical difference ultimately led to his second departure. "Craig Fuller did eventually rejoin the band but he just didn't stay very long and I think that pure prairie league was okay with that he was more into rock than they collectively wanted to be."

podcast.title: Vietnam War Conscientious Objector Status
podcast.body: Craig Fuller created significant issues for Pure Prairie League by claiming conscientious objector status for the Vietnam War draft. In 1973, he refused to report for the draft and was sentenced to six months in prison in Springfield, Missouri, followed by two years of service in an "alternative mental hospital." These legal problems were a direct cause for RCA dropping the band after their 1972 album "Bustin' Out." "Now granted Craig Fuller one of the band's co-founders created some issues because he claimed conscientious objector status with the draft board when he refused to report for the draft for the Vietnam war and was sentenced to six months in prison in Springfield, Missouri in 1973."
